name: Align Your Steps (AYS)
plain: Uses NVIDIA's published 10-step tables for SD1, SDXL and SVD (the file header links the source page), and log-linearly resamples them for any other step count. The denoise behaviour differs from BasicScheduler: it keeps only the last round(steps·denoise) steps rather than stretching to preserve the step count.
math:
Table τ (11 values). If steps+1 ≠ 11:
σ_i = exp(interp(i/steps, j/10, ln τ_rev)) reversed (piecewise-linear in ln σ).
Keep last round(steps·denoise)+1 values; last value forced to 0.
label: from code
surprise: The SVD table is 700→0.002, and all tables ignore the loaded model; picking the wrong model_type is not detected (no MODEL input, nodes_align_your_steps.py:34).
